topic: A person's invention is already patented by someone else
text: Rain slicks the streets, and the neon lights smear into streaks of color. I get a call, some guy thinks he's come up with something new, something revolutionary. Turns out, he's just another mark in a long line of dreamers, all of them chasing shadows. His invention, it's already patented—by someone else. Of course, he swears he didn't know, says he’s been working on it for years. I've heard it all before. People get desperate, they start seeing what they want to see. I tell him the world’s a tough place, especially when you’re up against someone with deeper pockets. He asks for help, and I can hear the shake in his voice. I tell him I’ll take a look, but I already know how this ends. People always want to believe in the new, in the fresh start, but most of the time, they're just spinning their wheels in the same old mud.
